subject: EU-US Data Transfer Evidence & DPF Supplement — HarborCare
body:
From: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@harborcare.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Vogel <anna.vogel@harborcare.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: EU-US transfer evidence (DPF supplemental)

Hi Kimberly / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. HarborCare Legal is compiling the packet we need to present to our regulators for an upcoming audit. Can you provide the technical mapping and evidence you would use to demonstrate an EU->US transfer is covered by the DPF (or equivalent safeguards) plus any operational controls (KMS, access controls, logging, key rotation cadence)?

Specifically:
- A short mapping tying processing activities to safeguards (e.g., SCCs/DPF clause IDs).
- Proof that encryption in transit and at rest is enabled and where keys are managed.
- Any export-control re-assertions (we need confirmation there are no restricted-exports processing requirements tied to this workload).

Appreciate a reply with attachments we can put straight into the compliance packet.

Best,
Tom
Senior Counsel, HarborCare

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@harborcare.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: EU-US transfer evidence (DPF supplemental)

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise technical mapping and our standard SCC+processor terms. Highlights below:

- Controller/Processor roles: Redwood operates as processor for hosted inference; customer is controller. DPA and processor addendum attached.
- Transfers: We support DPF equivalence via SCCs (we include a DPF supplement) and additional contractual guarantees. See page 2 of the attached PDF for clause links.
- Encryption: TLS1.2+ for in transit; AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) supported via KMS integration (we list GCP/AWS/Azure KMS connectors and HSM options).
- Logging & audit: Retention timelines configurable per customer; access is RBAC with time-limited emergency access and CLI audit trails.
- Export controls: Our platform does not perform geofencing of content for export-control restricted goods by default; we provide guidance for customers with export-controlled data to configure on-prem/private deployments.

I've looped in Laura and Marcus to confirm legal wording and the technical export-controls note. Attachments: redwood-dpf-technical-mapping-v1.xlsx, redwood-sccs-and-processor-terms-2027-09.pdf, export-controls-summary.txt

Next step: Laura will propose a short declarative statement you can include in your packet and Marcus can confirm technical fields in the mapping.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@harborcare.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: EU-US transfer evidence (DPF supplemental)

Tom, Kimberly —

Quick legal note to include:
1) Statement of scope: Our DPA and SCCs apply to personal data processed for the service described (inference, embeddings, logs used for billing). We do not assert a general adequacy decision beyond contractual safeguards.
2) Technical assurances: Encryption algorithms, KMS options, and audit capabilities are documented in the attached mapping. Where HarborCare elects BYOK, customer retains control of key material and we process under processor instructions only.
3) Export controls: Redwood confirms we do not ship controlled technical data to restricted jurisdictions as a services provider; customers using regulated datasets should consider Private deployment.

I will draft a short paragraph you can drop into your packet and send over a redline-friendly clause for any SCC tweaks.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@harborcare.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Request: EU-US transfer evidence (DPF supplemental)

Tom — attaching the mapping worksheet and a short README inside the sheet which maps each processing flow to the specific contractual clause and the technical artefact (logs, audit IDs, KMS key ARNs, region of primary storage). A couple of quick clarifications:
- Default hosted region: EU customers are stored primarily in eu-west-1 unless configured otherwise; backups and cold storage may be replicated to the US for resilience under the terms in the mapping.
- Key management: We support both Redwood-managed keys (rotated quarterly) and BYOK; with BYOK we do not have access to plaintext key material.
- Logging: Admin console and API logs retained by default for 90 days; extended retention is available via add-on. We include syslog/JSON export endpoints for audit ingestion.

If HarborCare wants, we can produce a short signed attestation with specific ARNs and region info for the environment that will host your workloads (this is useful for procurement/audit).

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@harborcare.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 17:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: EU-US transfer evidence (DPF supplemental)

Kimberly/Laura/Marcus — thank you, this is exactly what we needed. The HarborCare audit lead asked that we get an explicit attestation showing the primary storage region and the KMS key ARN for our environment. Can you provide that as a short signed PDF? Also confirm whether the export-control statement can be included verbatim in our packet.

If you can get the attestation to me by EOD Friday (10 Sept) that will keep our timeline intact.

Best,
Tom
Senior Counsel, HarborCare

---

[Attachment stubs: redwood-dpf-technical-mapping-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-sccs-and-processor-terms-2027-09.pdf (legal PDF), export-controls-summary.txt (plain text)]
